examples.input: Create a 1-month content calendar for a B2B SaaS company (HR software). We have a blog, LinkedIn, email newsletter, and a YouTube channel. Team: 1 content marketer, 1 designer. Goal: generate 30 MQLs from content this month.

business_goal_alignment.approach: Focus on bottom-of-funnel content that captures existing demand (comparison posts, buying guides, templates) rather than top-of-funnel awareness content

strategy.capacity_assessment: 1 content marketer + 1 designer = ~2 blog posts/week, 5 LinkedIn posts/week, 1 newsletter/week, 2 YouTube shorts/month. This is realistic and sustainable.

content.title: Complete Guide to HR Software for Growing Teams (50-200 employees)
content.cta: Free HR Software Comparison Checklist (gated PDF)

content.title: Post: 'The 3 HR tools every 50-person company actually needs (and the 5 they waste money on)'
Customer story: How [Customer] reduced onboarding time from 2 weeks to 2 days
Newsletter: 'HR planning for Q1: what to prioritize'
content.type: Newsletter with blog link + template offer

content.title: Hot take: 'Annual performance reviews are dead. Here's what replaces them.'
Repurpose: Key stats from the HR software comparison guide as a carousel
[Product] vs BambooHR vs Gusto: Honest Comparison for Small Teams
content.cta: Book a demo to see the difference

content.title: Post: Data from 500 HR leaders on what employees actually want in 2026
Newsletter: 'The comparison post you've been waiting for' + exclusive discount
60-sec product demo: Setting up your first onboarding workflow
Carousel: 5 red flags your HR software has outgrown your team

derivatives: Email newsletter feature: Key comparison table
YouTube Short: 60-sec 'which HR tool is right for you?' decision tree
LinkedIn text post: Hot take on why most comparison posts are biased
Twitter/X thread: 7 things to look for when evaluating HR software

sources: Gated template downloads (onboarding checklist, survey template, comparison checklist) — target: 15 MQLs
Blog → demo CTA clicks — target: 8 MQLs
Email newsletter → demo booking — target: 2 MQLs

examples.input: I'm a solo content creator running a personal finance blog. I also have an Instagram and a weekly newsletter. I can create about 5 hours of content per week. Help me plan a sustainable calendar.

output.capacity_reality_check: 5 hours/week means: 1 blog post (3 hrs writing + editing), 3 Instagram posts (30 min each), and 1 newsletter (1 hr). That's your max. Don't try to do more — consistency beats volume.

content_pillars.name: Money Fundamentals
content_pillars.description: Budgeting, saving, debt payoff — evergreen SEO content

content_pillars.name: Investing Simplified
content_pillars.description: Index funds, retirement accounts, compound interest

content_pillars.name: Money Mindset
content_pillars.description: Behavioral finance, emotional spending, personal stories

content_pillars.name: Tool Reviews
content_pillars.description: App reviews, bank comparisons — affiliate revenue potential

weekly_workflow.sunday: Batch content creation day (3 hours): Write blog post draft + create 3 Instagram graphics in Canva
weekly_workflow.monday: Publish blog post (30 min editing + SEO optimization). Schedule Instagram post #1.
weekly_workflow.wednesday: Instagram post #2. Write newsletter (1 hour) summarizing blog + adding personal commentary.
weekly_workflow.thursday: Send newsletter (morning). Engage with comments/DMs for 15 min.
weekly_workflow.friday: Instagram post #3. Engage with comments for 15 min.
weekly_workflow.weekend: No content work. Capture ideas in notes app for next week.

sustainability_tips: Never create more than 1 week ahead — burnout happens when you feel perpetually behind
Every blog post becomes: 1 newsletter summary + 3 Instagram posts (pull stats, quotes, tips). That's 5 pieces from 1 creation session.
Take 1 week off every 8 weeks. Schedule repurposed content that week — top-performing Instagram posts reshared, 'best of' newsletter.
Track what performs: if blog SEO posts drive 80% of your traffic, do more of those and fewer Instagram-only pieces

examples.input: Plan a content calendar around a product launch. We're releasing a new feature for our project management app in 6 weeks. Need pre-launch, launch, and post-launch content across blog, social, and email.

pre_launch_weeks_1_3.objective: Build awareness and anticipation. Educate the audience on the PROBLEM the feature solves before revealing the solution.

blog.title: Why [Problem] Is the #1 Complaint in Project Management (and What We're Doing About It)
blog.purpose: Problem awareness, SEO for problem keyword

blog.title: How 5 Teams Solved [Problem] (Before Our New Feature)
Coming Soon: A Better Way to [Solve Problem]
blog.purpose: Direct feature teaser with waitlist signup

social: Week 1: Poll — 'What's your biggest frustration with project management?' (engagement + research)
Week 2: Behind-the-scenes — 'Sneak peek of what our engineering team has been building for 6 months' (teaser photo/video)
Week 3: Countdown posts — 'Something big is coming in [X] days' with daily hints
email: Week 2: Segment existing users who've requested this feature → personal email from product manager
Week 3: Waitlist announcement to full list — 'Be the first to try our newest feature'

launch_week_4.objective: Maximum visibility. Every channel announces simultaneously.

day_by_day.action: Blog: Feature announcement post with demo video. Email: Launch announcement to full list. Social: Launch post on all platforms.
Blog: Tutorial — 'How to Use [Feature]: Complete Guide'. Social: User testimonial from beta tester.
Social: Short demo video (60 sec). Email: 'Did you see our new feature?' to non-openers from Monday.
Blog: Customer case study — 'How [Beta Customer] Uses [Feature] to Save 5 Hours/Week'. Social: Quote graphic from case study.
Social: Recap of launch week + thank you post. Email: 'What people are saying about [Feature]' — social proof roundup.

post_launch_weeks_5_6.objective: Drive adoption and collect user stories for ongoing marketing
content: Blog: Advanced tips — 'Pro Tips for [Feature]: 7 Things You Didn't Know You Could Do'
Social: User-generated content campaign — 'Show us how you use [Feature]' with a branded hashtag
Email: Feature adoption sequence to users who haven't tried it yet (3 emails over 2 weeks)
Social: Q&A Live/AMA about the feature — address questions and feedback publicly
